chunks: 3997 - And he, peace be upon him, said: "Every usury that people consumed out of ignorance, then they repented, it is accepted from them when repentance is recognized from them."

And he, peace be upon him, said: "If a man inherited wealth from his father and he knew that there was usury in that wealth, but it had become mixed in trade with other property, then it is lawful and good for him, so let him consume it. But if he knows a separated portion of it to be usury, then let him take his principal and return the usury."

key_terms.بِجَهَالَةٍ: in a state of ignorance of the ruling or reality
key_terms.تَابُوا: they repented and turned back from the act
key_terms.رَأْسَ مَالِهِ: his principal capital, excluding unlawful increase
key_terms.وَرِثَ: inherited wealth from a deceased relative

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on inherited wealth that contains mixed riba, and is repentance accepted for past usury done in ignorance?
ai.summary: This hadith explains rulings concerning usury when it was consumed in ignorance and followed by genuine tawbah. It also addresses inherited wealth containing mixed usury, permitting use of what is indistinguishably mixed while requiring the identified usurious portion to be returned.
